attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own newsletter post, offered as his observation of the period.

semantics.note: Keeps 'seemed' and 'increasingly'. 'Seemed' describes how the pattern looked, not a probability hedge. Leaving out the meme remark is fine.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: it asks whether announced supplier-investor/customer deals grew more prominent between Aug 2025 and Feb 2026. It does not require a rising share of realized financing, which the speaker never claimed. The window is inferred from context.

evidence.note: Sept 22, 2025 NVIDIA disclosure: planned investment of up to $100B in OpenAI, tied to OpenAI deploying NVIDIA systems. An announced circular deal inside the window.
Nov 18, 2025 Anthropic disclosure: NVIDIA and Microsoft investments paired with Anthropic's Azure/NVIDIA compute commitments. The pattern spreads to a second major lab inside the window.
Bank of England, Dec 2025: AI infrastructure was mostly funded by cash flows and equity. This limits a stronger 'dominant source' reading but does not measure the trend in circular deals.
Feb 1, 2026 Bloomberg: Huang calls the OpenAI deal non-binding, so it was announced, not completed. The report also notes concerns about circular deals over the past year.

reviews.rationale: Two major new announced investment-and-purchase deals fall in the window: NVIDIA-OpenAI in Sept 2025 and Microsoft/NVIDIA-Anthropic in Nov 2025. That meets the support condition for apparent growing prominence. The counterevidence (e3, e4) only rules out stronger readings: dominance of realized financing, or completed funding. It does not show such deals were shrinking. Supported on the plain reading.
